evidence: backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs:149 (check_redirect_uri_allowed) — the same-origin relative-path fast-path `if raw.starts_with('/') && !raw.starts_with("//") { return Ok(()) }` blocks protocol-relative `//evil.com` but NOT the backslash variant `/\evil.com` (nor `/\/evil.com`). A user-supplied redirect_uri of `/\evil.com` passes the allowlist as a 'relative path', is stored, re-validated at callback (still passes), and handed straight to `Redirect::temporary(&redirect_uri)` at routes/sso.rs:338, emitting `Location: /\evil.com`. Per the WHATWG URL spec browsers normalise backslashes to forward slashes for http(s) URLs, so `/\evil.com` resolves to `//evil.com` = `https://evil.com` -> open redirect on the post-login SSO flow (phishing / OAuth-code interception vector). The regression test block at routes/sso.rs:1681-1686 covers `//evil.com` but has NO backslash case, so CI is green. Fix: reject any raw whose first two chars normalise to a leading `//` (e.g. also block `starts_with("/\\")`), or parse-and-reject when url::Url::parse(raw) yields a host. Traced entry (login handler ~sso.rs:71 and callback ~sso.rs:204) -> validate -> Redirect; reachable in production.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/handlers/users/mod.rs:251 (UserHandler::login) — non-existent email and wrong password both correctly return the generic `"Invalid email or password"`, but a registered SSO-only account (user found, password_hash == None) returns a DISTINCT message via `.ok_or("Account uses SSO login")?`. routes/users.rs:204 (login handler) forwards that raw message verbatim as the 401 body. An attacker can therefore enumerate which emails are registered SSO accounts (distinct response = SSO account exists) — an account-existence disclosure that the generic path was specifically written to prevent. It also short-circuits before the argon2 verify, adding a timing side-channel. Fix: return the same generic `"Invalid email or password"` (log the SSO-account distinction server-side only).
